correctness.rationale: An integer generalized characteristic polynomial has linear coefficient ±2(n−1) for every tree. Odd n−1 and bipartite spectral symmetry forbid interior rational normalized-Laplacian eigenvalues with even reduced numerator. PST zero/2 projectors force equal vertex degrees and phase signs. Opposite classes give forbidden even-numerator phases; equal classes require a negative rational eigenvalue whose primitive integer eigenvector is constant modulo its numerator, so reflection forces that value to be 1. The difference of vertex states then identifies sibling leaves and leaves a residual positively signed interior phase, again forbidden. P2 is correctly excluded. A standalone exact-rational finite verifier supports, not substitutes for, the all-order proof.

value.rationale: The 2022 source explicitly conjectures that no tree except P2 and P3 admits normalized-Laplacian perfect state transfer. The present all-even-order theorem resolves a whole natural parity class without bounded order, degree or diameter, identifies the sharp P2 exception, and supplies a reusable two-adic spectral obstruction rather than an arbitrary finite calculation.
